name: Brow shaving / brow reshaping for tilt

image.caption: Brow shaving / brow reshaping for tilt

lead: Looksmaxxers reshape or trim their brows to make the eye area look more upward-angled, aiming for a positive tilt and a 'hunter eyes' look. The change is visible as soon as the hair is cut, and it costs almost nothing.

Changing the brow's outline changes the line the eye reads against, which proponents say alters the apparent angle of the eye. No studies were found testing whether trimming changes perceived tilt; the published research is on surgical brow shaping and lifting.

paras: People remove or trim hair with tweezers, wax, thread, scissors or a razor, and some redraw the shape with brow makeup. Because hair regrows, the shape is maintained with regular grooming, and many try small changes first.

Hair generally regrows, so changes are temporary, though over-trimming or over-plucking can leave gaps that take time to fill back in. Surgical brow shaping carries standard operative risks and is a separate matter from grooming.

angle.text: Trimming or reshaping the brows changes the line above the eye, which looksmaxxers use to make the eye area look more upward-tilted and 'hunter'-like. The change is cheap, reversible and visible right away. Its effect on perceived tilt has not been studied.

lead: Brow shaving or reshaping for tilt is the practice of trimming, shaving or redrawing the eyebrows, usually the inner head and the tail, so that the eye area reads as more upward-slanted and alert. People use it because the brow sits directly above the eye and frames it: a brow that rises toward the outer corner can make the eye line look more angled, a look associated in looksmaxxing talk with positive canthal tilt and "hunter eyes". In everyday grooming it is done by removing or trimming hair; Wikipedia lists tweezing, waxing, threading and trimming as common methods, and notes that some people shave the brows and draw them on [1].

The effect is visual and reversible, since hair regrows. Brow position can also be altered more permanently by cosmetic tattooing (microblading), eyebrow transplant, or surgical brow lifting, all of which Wikipedia describes [1].

Published research on the topic is surgical rather than cosmetic grooming. Plastic surgeons have described procedures that reshape brow position, including transcutaneous brow shaping and gliding brow lifts, in which the relationship between the medial and lateral portions of the brow is emphasised over overall height [2][3]. No studies of brow shaving or trimming for perceived eye tilt were found.

paras: Eyebrows are reported to protect the eye from sweat and debris and to be important in communicating emotion [1]. Brow shape has varied across cultures and eras, from high-painted brows in 8th-century Japan to thin brows in the 1920s and 1930s [1]. In appearance communities, brow shape is discussed as one factor in the impression of tilt, since an upward-slanting lateral brow can alter how the eye region reads.

Wikipedia describes the brow as an area of short terminal hairs above each eye that keeps sweat and debris out of the eye socket and serves in communication; it cites a 2018 study in Nature Ecology and Evolution suggesting eyebrows evolved mainly for communication, with a smooth forehead and mobile brows conveying subtle emotion [1]. The cosmetic literature on brow shape most often concerns women: a 2022 review noted that considerable effort has gone into defining the ideal female eye and brow while no such work exists for men, and described how men often develop upper lid hooding or brow ptosis with age [4].

Common grooming methods include tweezing, waxing, threading and trimming with small scissors, with permanent tinting and cosmetics also used to define the brows [1]. Brow hair that is removed can grow back, though the effects of repeated removal are not examined.

Wikipedia states that shaving brows bare, or shaving lines into them, was popular among some younger people in the 1990s and 2000s, and that cosmetic tattooing or microblading, in which pigment is placed in small cuts to mimic hair, became popular in the 21st century [1]. Eyebrow transplant uses follicles usually taken from the back of the head, with recovery resembling tattoo healing, and people with genetically thin or over-tweezed brows are considered typical candidates [1].

Surgeons authoring a 2017 paper argued that the relationship between the lateral and medial brow is aesthetically more important than absolute height, and described transcutaneous brow shaping as a way to shape the brow precisely and correct minor asymmetry [2]. A 2025 study described an endoscopic gliding forehead lift designed to lift both medial and lateral brow in Asian patients [3]. A 2022 review noted that no work has defined an ideal male eye and brow comparable to that for women [4].

The 2017 paper stated that, although various procedures raise the brow, transcutaneous brow shaping was in the authors' view the only technique enabling precise shaping and correction of minor asymmetries [2]. The 2025 endoscopic gliding forehead lift paper noted that the gliding browlift gained popularity for elevating the lateral brow, but that many Asian patients need both medial and lateral lifting to reach the desired shape [3]. A 2026 paper in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery described an extended gliding brow lift for brow and periorbital rejuvenation [5].

Brow fashion has changed across eras and has been tied to expectations about body hair. Wikipedia reports hikimayu in 8th-century Japan, in which natural brows were shaved or plucked and painted higher on the forehead, the removal of brows by some high-status women in the Elizabethan era, and thin, heavily plucked brows in the 1920s and 1930s [1]. Wikipedia gives the earliest published description of a brow lift as one from 1919 by the French surgeon Raymond Passot, and says that from the 1970s doctors began using botulinum toxin to raise brows [1].
No studies found on brow shaving or trimming for tilt. Related published work concerns surgical brow shaping and lifting, summarised above [2][3][4].
